proposal: Proposed by the writer on 2026-11-01 for the card 'The Criminal Mind · choose the adaptation scope' (project_id criminal_mind, controller_id baldadoon). The card shows one open question (the adaptation scope); the writer pass and the shot map delta hold eighteen author questions that are outstanding and invisible on the site. This delta asks the site to list them as review_requests on that card with their writer's defaults, to link the interview file that records the answers in the Hon interview's form, and to link the relay note Ziggy sends to the author. The three that shape the most work (B era and phone, K agency, O scope) come first; O is the card's own question. Not applied by the writer; CFA SITE INDEX applies or declines; CFA Nova wires the interview file to the interview section on her return.
appliesToCard: The Criminal Mind · choose the adaptation scope

linksAppend.label: Author questions, paste-ready relay note (18 questions; B, K, O first)
Author interview file (cfa-author-interview-v1; questions prepared, answers recorded here as they arrive)
Shot map delta v002 (the audit as actions)
Set camera maps v001 (the set-only round)

reviewRequestsAppend.title: A. Does the phone really ring?
reviewRequestsAppend.question: Nobody but John ever hears the voice in the phone; after line 972 the audience knows why. Should the vibration be staged as real (others could notice it), as John's alone, or left deliberately undecidable?
reviewRequestsAppend.whyItMatters: Touches every call scene; not blocking for scene 3.

reviewRequestsAppend.title: B. Era and the phone
reviewRequestsAppend.question: The phone slammed shut (818) and the cell phone of line 64 are the only form-factor details the script gives. The flip-phone years with a flip phone, or present day with a smartphone and an anonymous incoming call?
reviewRequestsAppend.writerDefault: period-neutral with the flip phone (G7); the set round keeps every cabin and desk free of modern screens either way
reviewRequestsAppend.whyItMatters: Shapes every phone insert, the car's dash, the office screens and the television; the blocked-number displays (248, 295) and the split screen (1690) pull two ways.

reviewRequestsAppend.title: C. Rating target
reviewRequestsAppend.question: The organs in silhouette (682), the jars (827), the shower (962), Jill shot (1471), Diego shot in the neck (1759), the boy's shot (36), the raid's two shootings (1827): implication over display, or as written?
reviewRequestsAppend.whyItMatters: Sets what the proof sequences may show; every set-only still already excludes blood and weapons.

reviewRequestsAppend.title: D. Two slurs
reviewRequestsAppend.question: Line 606 (Diego about his own people) and line 1260 (John at Fox): kept as written in the film, or not? The record keeps them verbatim either way.

reviewRequestsAppend.title: E. Jack's origin
reviewRequestsAppend.question: Why does the second state have a British delivery? The screenplay gives no reason (John raises it at 807; Jack deflects at 810). Keep it unexplained, or is there a reason the film should plant?
reviewRequestsAppend.whyItMatters: Voice casting must be British by line 807 at the latest either way.

reviewRequestsAppend.title: F. Who fires the shot that kills Jill
reviewRequestsAppend.question: Jack says 'I'm sick of this' and the gun goes off (1469 to 1471); on the roof Johnny claims her (1590, 1625, 1634). Which state is on camera at 1471?
options: no state: the body goes still and silent
reviewRequestsAppend.writerDefault: the body goes still and silent for the shot, no state speaking, so the roof's claim lands as the explanation
reviewRequestsAppend.whyItMatters: Decides the key frame of scene 36 and the gun's travel to the bed (1508) and the roof (1715).

reviewRequestsAppend.title: G. The ammonia
reviewRequestsAppend.question: John tells Jen that Jack said ammonia (154) though Jack never did (114 to 120); Diego confirms ammonia at 222. An intended slip (John knows because he was there), or an oversight?
options: oversight, to be repaired by the author
reviewRequestsAppend.writerDefault: intended, played straight with no underline, so it works on a second viewing
reviewRequestsAppend.whyItMatters: Blocking for scene 4; the plot is not repaired by the writer.

reviewRequestsAppend.title: H. The quality of the cuts
reviewRequestsAppend.question: 'Clean cut' (51), 'aren't as good as we thought they were' (638), 'so much for him not knowing what he was doing' (870): deliberate (the briefing was wrong), or an oversight?
reviewRequestsAppend.writerDefault: play each as written; no line changed
reviewRequestsAppend.whyItMatters: Affects how the silhouette at 682 is lit and read.

reviewRequestsAppend.title: I. The timeline
reviewRequestsAppend.question: Seven years with Steele (1767); four months earlier (1806); a month before the killings (1803); the boy was fifteen and John is thirty-three. Consistent as read, but tight against five victims across the film's weeks. Does the author want the dates fixed?
reviewRequestsAppend.whyItMatters: The flashback's time of day and the day count across scenes 8 to 10 depend on it.

reviewRequestsAppend.title: J. Johnny's origin, told several ways
reviewRequestsAppend.question: Johnny says he was created the instant the boy fired (1603) and that he took over again at the raid (1895); Steele recounts the boy's cover story that a man named Johnny did it (1773); Fox says the personalities came out only recently. Which account does the film believe, or do all stand as unreliable?
reviewRequestsAppend.writerDefault: all three stand; none is confirmed on screen
reviewRequestsAppend.whyItMatters: Shapes the coda and the flashback's staging (40-07).

reviewRequestsAppend.title: K. The agency
reviewRequestsAppend.question: State Police (525, 1809), a PD garage (325), a precinct (516), barracks and a sled (394), a federal case over state lines (379). One agency name for the signage, badges and cars?
reviewRequestsAppend.writerDefault: Massachusetts State Police throughout, since the screenplay names it twice and the others are colloquial
reviewRequestsAppend.whyItMatters: Signage, badges, cars and the precinct's exterior; the set round shoots everything unlettered meanwhile.

reviewRequestsAppend.title: L. The witness who saw John leave
reviewRequestsAppend.question: The witness (1203 to 1215) is never resolved and the alibi gap stands (home at 10:00, seen at 8:30 to 9:00). Keep it open as written, or add a beat that answers it?
reviewRequestsAppend.whyItMatters: A new beat would be new coverage.

reviewRequestsAppend.title: M. Props that contradict
reviewRequestsAppend.question: What John tells the agents about the night before (no cigarettes on him, 1165) against what the body did (the butt pocketed at 80, the one lit at 100, the one found at the scene, 1147 to 1156); the gun left on the bed (1508) against the revolver drawn on the roof (1715). Keep as written (the writer tracks them in continuity notes) or resolve?
reviewRequestsAppend.writerDefault: keep; the continuity notes carry them

reviewRequestsAppend.title: N. The ending's tone
reviewRequestsAppend.question: The pinch (1919) and the nurse's shrug end the film on Johnny's amusement. Keep, or end on the open eyes (1877)?
reviewRequestsAppend.whyItMatters: The last shot of the coda.

reviewRequestsAppend.title: O. Screen length (for Ziggy and Baldadoon together)
reviewRequestsAppend.question: The whole screenplay as one film (the writer pass, Part 9, estimates its length), or a contained excerpt first? This is the site card's open question, choose the adaptation scope.
reviewRequestsAppend.writerDefault: none; this is the one decision that sets the size of everything after the first proof sequence

reviewRequestsAppend.title: P. Time of day of scenes 8, 10 and 20 (new, from the corrections pass)
reviewRequestsAppend.question: Scene 8's slug says Night against 'still dark out' and the sunrise at 291; scene 10 follows the sunrise; scene 20's slug says Day against 'home at night' and the 10:05 clock. Pre-dawn, day, day as the writer has lit them, or otherwise?
reviewRequestsAppend.whyItMatters: The bedroom's dawn state and the office's light.

reviewRequestsAppend.title: Q. The coda's staging (new)
reviewRequestsAppend.question: In scene 41, do Jack and Johnny speak through the body on camera, the face changing state, or as inner voices while the body lies still?
reviewRequestsAppend.writerDefault: on camera, the face changing state, since the nurse reacts to nothing and the pinch (1919) is physical

reviewRequestsAppend.title: R. Which hand is cuffed (new)
reviewRequestsAppend.question: Line 1877 says 'hand cuffed' and never names the hand; the free hand moves at 1919. Which hand is cuffed to the rail?
options: writer decides with the bed geometry
reviewRequestsAppend.writerDefault: the writer fixes it with the bed geometry: the cuff on the window side, the nurse's working side toward the door
reviewRequestsAppend.whyItMatters: The hospital set's positions (HOS-P02 and HOS-P03) swap if reversed.

nextText: Read the notes and choose the adaptation scope (O). Eighteen writer's questions are outstanding; B (era and phone) and K (agency) shape the set round. Answers return through Ziggy; the writer records them.
